label: AML/CFT Data-Quality Governance
description: Field-level data-quality governance for AML/CFT programmes: beneficial-owner completeness, screening-list timeliness, CDD field accuracy, risk-tiered retention, and end-to-end data lineage for AMLA direct data requests. Applies ISO 8000 and BCBS 239 dimensions to AML data.

claudeKnowledge.description: AMLR (EU) 2024/1624; AMLA Regulation (EU) 2024/1620; AMLD6 (EU) 2024/1640; TFR (EU) 2023/1113; GDPR (EU) 2016/679; ISO 8000 (data quality); BCBS 239 (risk data aggregation); ISO 20022; EBA Guidelines on ML/TF risk factors; FATF Recommendations (2023).

guidedInputs.label: Known Data-Quality Issues or Concerns
guidedInputs.description: Describe any known data-quality problems, audit findings, system-migration legacy, or supervisory feedback on data.
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g. UBO percentages frequently null on legacy onboardings; sanctions list refresh is a manual weekly batch; customer addresses inconsistent between core banking and the screening engine; no documented lineage from source system to the screening payload...

exampleInput: We are a Finnish payment institution (~200 staff) preparing for AMLR application and likely selection for AMLA-coordinated supervision. We hold roughly 40,000 active business customers onboarded across three different KYC systems over the last decade, plus a 2021 core-banking migration that we suspect dropped or truncated several beneficial-ownership fields. Sanctions and PEP lists are refreshed by a nightly batch, but adverse-media is a quarterly manual pull. We have never produced an end-to-end lineage diagram showing how a UBO ownership percentage travels from the source registry extract into the screening payload and the customer risk score. Assess our AML/CFT data quality at field level — beneficial-owner completeness, CDD field accuracy, screening-list timeliness, risk-tiered retention against the AMLR 5-year rule versus our GDPR minimisation baseline, and the data lineage we would need to satisfy an AMLA direct data request. Produce a data-readiness scorecard and a prioritised remediation list. Known weak spots: UBO percentages are frequently null on pre-2021 records and we cannot currently evidence when a given sanctions match was screened against which list version.

exampleValues.known_concerns: UBO ownership percentages frequently null on pre-2021 core-banking-migration records. Adverse-media screening is a quarterly manual pull; only sanctions/PEP are nightly. No end-to-end lineage from source registry extract to screening payload to risk score. Cannot evidence which sanctions list version a historic match was screened against.
